drhp.business: Technocrats Plasma Systems Limited is an engineering-led manufacturer of plasma cutting machines, welding equipment and customised automation systems for metal fabrication and related industries in India. Its products are used by customers across automotive, construction, shipbuilding, heavy engineering and general manufacturing sectors, and its activities span system configuration, detailed engineering, fabrication, assembly, testing, installation/commissioning support and after-sales service and spares.
drhp.expansion: Company intends to strengthen its manufacturing base at the Existing Premises (Unit-I and Unit-II at Gaodevi Industrial Estate, Sativali, Vasai East) using IPO Net Proceeds to purchase and install additional plant and machinery for manufacturing plasma cutting machines, welding equipment and customised automation systems.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Currently dependent on external suppliers for raw materials and certain precision components, without long-term supply agreements or fixed terms of trade with most suppliers (top 10 suppliers contributed 93.50% of purchases in FY26, 93.12% in FY25, 43.63% in FY24). IPO capex (per Objects of the Offer) is aimed at augmenting production capacity and is expected to reduce dependence on external vendors for certain precision components, with in-house production of critical components and tooling expected to improve cost efficiencies and operating margins. Company operates a business-to-business (B2B) model supplying cutting, welding and automation equipment to fabrication shops, OEMs and industrial customers across heavy fabrication/engineering, automotive/auto components, infrastructure/construction equipment, shipbuilding, steel service centres and process industries; customers span 22 states and 2 countries. Revenue from repeat orders vs. new customers: FY26 Rs.2,48,311 thousand repeat / Rs.10,64,778 thousand new customers (total Rs.13,13,090 thousand); FY25 Rs.1,36,698 thousand repeat / Rs.3,56,870 thousand new (total Rs.4,93,568 thousand); FY24 Rs.55,231 thousand repeat / Rs.5,392 thousand new (total Rs.60,623 thousand).

overview.business_model: The company designs, engineers, fabricates and supplies plasma cutting machines, welding equipment and customised automation systems, and earns revenue from equipment sales together with technical consultancy, installation/commissioning support, operator familiarisation, after-sales service and supply of spares and consumables over the equipment's life.

genesis.founding_story: Founded by Arun Kumar, a former Scientific Officer at the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Mumbai, who worked on plasma and laser technologies for the Government of India before founding the Company; began indigenous design and supply of inverter-based TIG welding systems and air plasma cutting machines in 1996.

concerns_observed: Related-party purchases of raw materials, manpower and services from Techno Dyne, proprietor Sudhir Kumar Sharma (a Director's relative), totalled Rs.116.84 crore in FY26, Rs.45.15 crore in FY25 and Rs.2.45 crore in FY24 -- comparable to nearly the entire disclosed raw-material cost base each year.
Customer concentration remains high: top-10 customers were 83.89% of revenue in FY25 and 62.61% in FY26; top-5 customers were 70.58% in FY25.
Supplier concentration: top-10 suppliers accounted for 93.50% (FY26) and 93.12% (FY25) of purchases, with no long-term supply agreements or fixed trade terms with most suppliers.
Operating cash flow was negative in both FY26 (-Rs.11.66 crore) and FY25 (-Rs.5.05 crore), with growth instead funded by financing inflows (+Rs.13.07 crore FY26, +Rs.5.18 crore FY25).

Installed manufacturing capacity utilisation was only 50.08% (FY26), 58.38% (FY25) and 16.05% (FY24) per Chartered Engineer Garg and Associates' certification, even as further capacity is being added from IPO proceeds.
Revenue is geographically concentrated in Maharashtra and Gujarat (75.91% in FY26, 93.12% in FY25), with exports nil in FY26 versus 0.55%-0.60% in prior years.
Employee attrition of 38.81% (FY26) and 60.00% (FY25) against a base of only 40 permanent employees as of June 30, 2026, with no succession policy disclosed.
Personal guarantees of Promoters Arun Kumar and Vandana Sharma secure a significant portion of the Company's bank borrowings (total debt Rs.14.73 crore as of FY26).
Outstanding litigation includes a Rs.58.91 lakh commercial suit (Maurer-Sanfield India Ltd., next hearing August 25, 2026) and 8 tax proceedings against the Company totalling Rs.285.64 lakh.

verdict.our_read: Technocrats Plasma Systems is a 30-year-old Vasai (Maharashtra) manufacturer of plasma cutting, welding and automation equipment whose revenue surged from Rs.6.06 crore (FY24) to Rs.131.31 crore (FY26) largely on a handful of customers and near-total dependence on one related-party supplier (Techno Dyne, Rs.116.84 crore of FY26 purchases), even as none of the IPO's plant-and-machinery capex orders have been placed and promoters' average share cost (Rs.5.09-6.04) sits far below the yet-to-be-fixed issue price.
post_listing_commitments: Entire Net Proceeds toward plant & machinery (Rs.8.79 crore) proposed for deployment in FY2026-27, with orders to be placed within 1 month of receipt of Net Proceeds, delivery in 6 months, installation in 3 months, and operational status within 2 months thereafter.
Rs.40 crore of Net Proceeds earmarked for long-term working capital, phased as Rs.20 crore in Fiscal 2027 and Rs.20 crore by December 31, 2027 (Fiscal 2028).

Promoters' minimum contribution of 35,10,500 Equity Shares (27.26% of pre-Issue capital, held by Arun Kumar and Vandana Sharma) locked in for 3 years from the date of IPO allotment under Regulation 238 of SEBI ICDR Regulations, 2018.
red_flags: Statutory auditor issued a Basis for Qualified Opinion for FY2022-23 on non-confirmation/reconciliation of trade receivables, trade payables, advances and loans, and improper inventory records for raw materials and semi-finished goods.

Three pending Section 454 (Companies Act) adjudication applications for technical non-compliance: Section 42(4) escrow-to-current-account transfer timing (filed December 29, 2025); Section 12(3)(a) non-display of company details at two warehouses (filed May 21, 2026); Section 4(1)(c) Objects Clause not covering all business activities (filed June 4, 2026).

SEBI rejected the Company's exemption application (rejection letter dated January 13, 2026) for non-cooperating Promoter Group member Geeta Singh (Promoter's sister), who did not respond to information requests; her disclosures are based on public information only.

100% of the Rs.8.96 crore plant-and-machinery capex (10 items -- Procal Solution, Laser Science Services Pvt Ltd, Jayco Hoist & Cranes MFG. Co, etc.) has no orders placed as of the RHP date, and deployment of Net Proceeds has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.

Promoters' average cost of acquisition (Arun Kumar Rs.5.09/share, Vandana Sharma Rs.6.04/share) sits far below the yet-to-be-determined SME issue price, alongside a 6:1 bonus issue (1,10,40,000 shares) allotted August 12, 2025 -- months before the IPO -- that expanded the paid-up base shortly ahead of listing.
History of 26 delayed statutory ROC filings (Form 5, Form 66, AOC 4, MGT 7/7A, MGT 14, DIR 12, DPT 3, SH-7, GNL 2) between 2007 and 2025, each regularised with late fees of Rs.500-Rs.7,200.
strengths_observed: Revenue grew from Rs.6.06 crore (FY24) to Rs.49.36 crore (FY25) to Rs.131.31 crore (FY26), a roughly 365% two-year revenue CAGR, with FY26 EBITDA margin of 20.02% and PAT margin of 11.37%.
Return on net worth of 56.10% (FY26), 90.21% (FY25) and 83.76% (FY24).

30-year operating history (incorporated November 1, 1994) founded by Arun Kumar, a former Scientific Officer at BARC, with two 2025 Technology Transfer Agreements -- one with AIC RRCAT PI-HUB Foundation (RRCAT, Indore) for fiber laser material-processing technology and one with BARC for air plasma incinerators.
Working-capital cycle improved sharply: debtor days fell from 197 (FY24) to 58 (FY26); inventory days fell from 947 (FY24) to 123 (FY26); creditor days fell from 152 to 35.
Customer concentration eased in the latest year: top-10 customer share fell to 62.61% (FY26) from 83.89% (FY25), and repeat-customer revenue rose to Rs.2.48 crore in FY26 from Rs.0.55 crore in FY24.
Export track record across 7 countries since 2007 (Oman, Nigeria, Kuwait, Uganda, Bhutan, Greece, Cameroon-2024) and a domestic footprint spanning 22 states.
